samples.summary: Refactor routes the unbounded, clipboard-controlled paste grid through `rangeOf`, whose `Math.min(...rows)` spread throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` on large pastes (untrusted-input DoS)
samples.evidence: The diff replaces the explicit bounding-box loop in `selectPastedRange` with `const [from, to] = rangeOf(grid)` (sheet.ts:2555). `rangeOf` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:19-26) builds `rows`/`cols` arrays and spreads them into `Math.min(...)`/`Math.max(...)`. V8 caps spread/apply argument counts at roughly 65k-125k elements; beyond that the call throws `RangeError`. The grid reaching this call is built with no size limit at all: `paste` -> `string2grid(this.activeCell, text)` -> `parseTsvRows(text)` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/grids.ts:113-126) emits one Map entry per TSV field with no cap, and the html path (`html2grid`) is likewise uncapped. Attack/vector: a page (or any app) places a >65k-cell TSV on the clipboard — e.g. 700 rows x 100 columns, an ordinary spreadsheet paste — and the user presses Ctrl+V. `selectPastedRange` is the last statement of `paste`, executed AFTER `store.endBatch()` has committed the writes, so the exception propagates into the view's catch (packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4940 and packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:728), which only `console.error`s — `clearCopyBuffer()` and `render()` are skipped, leaving the document mutated but the canvas showing stale content and the copy buffer live. The previous loop-based implementation had no such ceiling, and `rangeOf` had no other production caller (grep shows sheet.ts:2555 is its only non-test use), so this is newly reachable with clipboard-sized input.

samples.summary: Paste writes merges into the shared document without the bounds/validity checks the backend enforces in `parseMerges`, so a paste near the grid edge can persist merge state the API layer would reject
samples.evidence: `applyPasteMerges` calls `this.store.setMerge(merge.anchor, merge.span)` (sheet.ts:2483) with an anchor computed as `sourceAnchor + delta` (sheet.ts:2415-2418) and the span copied verbatim from the copy buffer. Nothing on this path re-applies the validation `mergeSelection` gets from `canMergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4595-4612: no frozen-pane crossing, no overlap) nor the grid-bounds rule the server enforces for the same data in `packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:135-147` (`anchor.r <= MaxRows`, `rs <= MaxRows - anchor.r + 1`). Because the frontend store writes merges straight into the Yorkie CRDT (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:961-982), that REST validation is bypassed entirely: pasting a copied 3-row merged block onto the last row, or across a frozen-pane boundary, persists a merge that `PUT /merges` would 400 on, and that every collaborator then loads and renders. Impact is document-integrity/consistency rather than privilege escalation; the same gap already exists on the `moveRangeTo` path (sheet.ts:2703), which this change generalizes to paste.

samples.summary: The internal-paste branch is still selected purely by clipboard-text equality, but now performs destructive structural mutation (creating merges and deleting cell data underneath them), widening what a spoofed clipboard can trigger
samples.evidence: `if (this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text)` (sheet.ts:2233) is the only trust check distinguishing an internal paste from foreign clipboard content. Before this change that branch only rewrote values with relocated formulas; after it, the same branch runs `applyPasteMerges` -> `clearCellsUnderMerge`, which issues `store.delete(ref)` for pre-existing cells covered by the re-created merge (sheet.ts:2542) and deletes spill ghosts (sheet.ts:2531). A page that can write the OS clipboard on a user gesture and can guess/observe the exact text the user last copied (e.g. text it itself supplied into the sheet) can therefore make Ctrl+V destroy destination cells that were not represented in the clipboard text at all. Damage stays inside the document the user is already editing and within the translated source range, so this is amplification rather than a privilege boundary break — reported for completeness because the destructive surface of a clipboard-string-matched branch grew here.

samples.summary: `clearCellsUnderMerge` silently deletes cell contents in filtered/hidden rows covered by a pasted merge, destroying data the user cannot see or audit
samples.evidence: `clearCellsUnderMerge` iterates `mergeCoveredSrefs(anchor, span)` (sheet.ts:2512) and deletes every non-written cell in the block, with no consideration of `filterRange`/hidden rows (`recomputeFilterHiddenRows` is only invoked afterwards, sheet.ts:2369-2371). A paste that re-creates a multi-row merged block over a filtered region therefore erases values in rows the viewport is not showing, with no confirmation and no refusal. The equivalent loop existed for drag-move, but paste is a far more frequent gesture and the destination footprint (translated source range) can extend past what the user sees. Integrity/blast-radius flavoured; flagged at low confidence because the hidden-row semantics of merges elsewhere may already intend this.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is real and I confirmed every technical element: rangeOf (coordinates.ts:18-27) spreads one argument per grid entry into Math.min/Math.max; selectPastedRange (sheet.ts:2552-2555) is its only production caller; string2grid (grids.ts:113-126) caps nothing; and selectPastedRange runs at sheet.ts:2377 after endBatch (sheet.ts:2372-2374), with only a console.error handler at worksheet.ts:4940-4942 that skips clearCopyBuffer()/render(). So it is not 'not-present' and not 'already-guarded'. It is, however, out of scope for the Security lens: the sole entry point reads the user's own clipboard in the user's own tab (worksheet.ts:4910-4937, spreadsheet.ts:698-728), so attacker and victim are the same principal and no privilege boundary is crossed. There is no authorization gate, secret, injection sink, crypto/signature check, SSRF, deserialization, or path traversal involved — the impact is an unhandled RangeError leaving a stale canvas, i.e. a client-side robustness/availability defect. The same failure fires on an ordinary large legitimate paste, which marks it as a correctness bug; the rubric explicitly defers general logic bugs, and the correctness lens already owns this exact issue (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:10, verifier-confirmed), so refuting it here does not remove it from the merge gate.
